original_acceptance: Ensure changes to native code, wrappers, publisher, evidence and benchmark helpers select the necessary checks; inspect combined workflow coverage.

findings.finding: Main CI has no path filter for pull requests targeting release/3.2. It collects the tests directory, partitions all collected nodes into 96 affinity-aware shards with explicit flattened-length and node-ID-set equality checks, and runs the shards on Ubuntu with Python3.12. Production Ruff/format and basedpyright are explicit gates.
findings.limit: Collection on Linux does not execute Windows-skipped cases or establish other Python versions. Inspection did not execute the planner, and new final-source node membership still requires its actual test-plan record. These checks are described as implemented; this review does not infer multiset uniqueness from length/set equality alone.

findings.finding: Native wheel CI is unconditional for release/3.2 pull requests and has four platform jobs. Rust runtime matches rust/**, guard/**, ci/native_runtime/** and selected native scripts/dependency/support paths. The integrated deadline paths select these workflows.
findings.limit: The native-wheel fixed Python test lists are not the complete Python suite. The current PR's cumulative diff contains Rust changes; its observed workflow selection alone cannot prove future isolated Python changes are covered.

findings.finding: The ordinary full Python suite is Linux/Python3.12. The selected RSP100 cohorts' four-platform/declared-version proof currently comes from a temporary exact-source validation branch. Pyproject declares requires-python>=3.10 and classifiers3.10–3.14.
findings.resolution: Prepare scoped permanent request-risk workflow/portable runner wiring with actual host/interpreter/source admission and meaningful once-only/invalidation controls, while retaining exact candidate binding in the separate one-off driver.
findings.status: Concrete implementation assigned to the RSP100 owner; no source delta or passing run is claimed by this review.

findings.finding: Linux's general pytest collection may skip Windows-specific file behavior, and the existing native Windows lanes use fixed test lists. The successful17-case Ex mechanism remains an isolated CI probe; a coherent product path needs its original real Windows controls wired into the ordinary selected workflow.
findings.resolution: Include necessary permanent actual-product Windows test invocation and dependency selectors in the forthcoming coherent reader/writer proposal, preserving old success/error/sharing/audit/cleanup controls.
findings.status: Assigned to the Windows owner; no product mechanism or ordinary CI invocation is claimed by this review.

findings.finding: Some scheduling-sensitive/stress jobs are schedule-or-dispatch only, and release/signing/publication jobs have additional conditions. An ordinary pull-request success cannot be credited as execution of these jobs or full installed/performance/rollback qualification.
findings.limit: Raw job condition expressions are retained. This source inspection does not evaluate external secrets/variables or claim their availability.
